correctness.rationale: The rectangular character calculation is correct. For a uniform additive input channel, nontrivial characters diagonalize the conditional-expectation operator, so maximal correlation is the largest nonzero Fourier coefficient of the mask. For R=UV, conditioning on U gives coefficient q^{-r rank(H)}, hence exactly q^{-r}. For the rank ball, the block decomposition around a nonzero H reduces the character sum to q^r times the rank-r count in the (m-1)x(n-1) corner; rank-one H attains the absolute upper bound, giving the exact stated ratio and its q^{-r} bound. The kernel-size test statistic is invariant under invertible left/right transformations, and direct pair counting gives the displayed correlation lower bound for every fixed-rank K; averaging over random K preserves the bound. The two-input maximal-correlation identity follows from tensor-product singular values. The DP entropy argument is valid using the conditional largest-atom inequality together with Han/Shearer subadditivity and the support-size bound for rank-r matrices. A fresh exact F_2 enumeration independently reproduced the rank-ball values 3/11, 9/25, 21/53 and 3/43 and the 3x4 rank-one kernel correlation 41/105.

originality.rationale: Cohen--D'Oliveira--Sprintson formulate the multiplication protocol for rectangular products, but their abstracted maximal-correlation theorems and asymptotic converse are stated for independent uniform n x n inputs. The audited record gives exact dependence on both rectangular dimensions, an exact rank-ball character formula, a finite-aspect-ratio converse, and the matching rectangular DP obstruction. Targeted searches for these rectangular formulas did not locate a prior privacy theorem, although related character sums are classical in bilinear-forms association schemes.

scientific_value.rationale: The extension removes a square-matrix restriction from the privacy theory of a protocol that is intrinsically rectangular. Exact formulas show that factor-mask leakage remains dimension-free at q^{-r}, identify the weaker mask budget in two-input multiplication, and quantify how aspect ratio changes the universal converse and DP obstruction. These are operationally relevant generalizations rather than a notational change.

limitations: Maximal-correlation statements assume uniform inputs and input-independent additive masks.
The factor-two converse is stated only for r<=min(m,n)-2; the exact correlation identity can be weaker near full rank.

Classical rank-metric association-scheme literature may contain equivalent character-sum identities, so originality is claimed for the rectangular privacy theorem and consequences rather than the underlying finite-field harmonic analysis.
The DP bound is an impossibility statement for rank-bounded additive masks, not a general privacy lower bound for interactive or computational protocols.
